title: How to Choose an AI Writing Tool: A Practical Checklist
seoTitle: Choosing an AI Writing Tool: A Checklist
description: A short, concrete checklist for picking an AI writing tool you will still like after the trial month: tasks, limits, data, and exit routes.
author: AIVOXFLOW Editorial
disclosure: Desk research based on official product documentation and pricing pages checked on 2026-10-15. No hands-on testing was performed for this article.
body:
Most people choose an AI writing tool the wrong way: they pick the one with the loudest launch video. Three months later the subscription is unused. This checklist takes ten minutes and saves a billing cycle.

## Start with your task, not the model

Write down the three things you would actually use the tool for every week. Be specific:

- "Draft weekly client emails" — a real task
- "Write better" — not a task, and it never ends in a decision

Tools differ in emphasis: some are strongest at long-form drafting, others at quick answers with web sources, others at working inside documents you already use. Your task list decides the shortlist more than any benchmark.

## Check the free tier honestly

Nearly every major assistant now offers a free tier. We verified current free plans on official pricing pages for [ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/), [Claude](https://claude.ai/), and [Gemini](https://gemini.google.com/) at the time of writing (see our [AI tools index](/tools/) for dated verification notes). Use it for a full week on your real tasks. Watch for:

- Message or usage caps that hit mid-task
- Whether your required features (file uploads, images, long documents) are limited or absent on the free plan
- Whether the paid tier's limits are published clearly or hidden

## Read the data terms before you paste anything

Two questions, both answerable from the vendor's own privacy or trust pages:

1. Is content you enter used to train models, and can you opt out?
2. How long are conversations retained?

If you plan to paste client material, contracts, or code, this section of the checklist outranks writing quality.

## Price the second year, not the first

Promotional pricing, annual-only discounts, and currency differences make first-year costs misleading. Check the standard monthly price, then multiply by twelve. A tool that is twice as expensive but replaces two others may still win, but make that trade consciously.

## Plan your exit before you commit

Can you export your conversations and documents? If the answer is no, your work lives inside someone else's product. Favor tools with export options, or accept the lock-in knowingly.

## The five-line version

1. List your three real weekly tasks.
2. Test free tiers on those tasks for a week.
3. Read the data terms.
4. Price year two.
5. Check you can get your work out.

## Sources and further reading

- [ChatGPT pricing (official)](https://chatgpt.com/pricing)
- [Claude pricing (official)](https://www.anthropic.com/pricing)
- [Gemini subscriptions (official)](https://gemini.google/subscriptions/)

*Pricing and limits change often — verify on official pages before buying.*
